claims.text: Applying a chromium-rich coating to boride-based components improves their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion relative to uncoated components.
The chromium-rich coating remains effective during exposure to molten aluminum at temperatures below 700°C.
A chromium-rich coating reacts with oxygen to form a chromium oxide layer.
The chromium oxide layer is protective against molten-aluminum attack.
The chromium oxide layer prevents molten aluminum from contacting the underlying boride-based component.
Preventing contact between molten aluminum and the boride-based component suppresses corrosion of the component.
Temperatures above 700°C lie outside the proposed effective operating range of the coating.
Exposure to corrosive substances other than molten aluminum lies outside the proposed effective operating range.
Coating effectiveness may depend on the composition and microstructure of the boride-based component and the coating.
